verdict_reason:
APPROVED at 47dc1b77. The delta since my reviewed sha 7cff6284 is test-only and carries no security impact; every conclusion of the primary review survives unchanged, and the one substantive delta change makes the suite stricter rather than weaker.

=== DELTA REVIEW (7cff6284..47dc1b77) ===

SCOPE CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS DECLARED. `git diff --name-only 7cff6284..47dc1b77` returns exactly three paths: the superseded verdict handoff under specs/releases/_archive/0.5.3/verdicts/, specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl, and tests/unit/features/specs/test_tree5_shipped_history.py. Decisively, `git diff --name-only 7cff6284..47dc1b77 -- dadaia_workspace/` returns EMPTY -- not one production file changed, so no production attack surface moved and nothing in my module-by-module review of the primary range needs revisiting.

THE TEST CHANGE STRENGTHENS THE ASSERTION -- IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF SILENCING. Two filter lines change from `"releases/AGENTS.md" in (i.path or "")` to `PurePath(i.path or "").as_posix().endswith("releases/AGENTS.md")`, with `PurePath` added to an existing pathlib import. This is a substring match becoming a separator-normalised SUFFIX match: strictly narrower, so it cannot match more than before, and it removes a false-negative class. The bug it fixes matters for test integrity: on Windows, `issue.path` is an OS-native absolute path with backslashes, so the posix substring never matched and the filtered list came back empty. In the two repaired tests the empty list made `assert scoped and scoped[0].fixable` FAIL outright (the CI failure), while the related negative assertion would have passed for the wrong reason. Restoring a real match on Windows RESTORES genuine coverage on that platform -- the reverse of the mandatory REQUEST_CHANGES trigger 'a test disabled to hide a live failure'. Nothing was skipped, xfailed or quarantined; no assertion was deleted or loosened.

I CHECKED WHETHER THE FIX WAS INCOMPLETE, AND IT IS NOT. The same module retains one more path filter that was NOT converted (line 190, the exclusion test, filtering on the needle `"memory"`). I verified rather than assumed: that needle contains no path separator, so substring matching behaves identically under both separator conventions and it cannot yield the platform-dependent false negative this bug is about. The two lines that needed conversion are exactly the two that were converted.

DELTA SECRETS AND PRIVATE-NAME SCAN -- CLEAN. Scanning ONLY the delta's added lines for operator-home absolute path prefixes, credential keywords, PEM key headers, RFC1918 and private-IP literals, personal e-mail domains, AWS access-key IDs, GitHub and Slack token shapes, the operator's name, and every sibling repo slug on the denylist returns ZERO hits in the two content paths (the BUGS.jsonl record and the test file). The only matches anywhere in the delta come from the superseded verdict handoff's own prose, where the matched words are quoted grep PATTERNS and the name of the scan engine -- detector vocabulary, never credential material. The appended BUGS.jsonl record parses as valid JSON with 26 fields and carries only a bug id, a test-file component path, a public CI run number, a public PR number, a runner label, severity LOW, surface 'tests', status 'resolved' and diff_direction 'net-neutral'. No absolute local path, no host, no IP, no private name, no secret -- the registration redaction discipline was followed.

SUITE RE-RUN AT THE NEW HEAD. The repaired module passes 8/8. The security-relevant selector (secret|privacy|injection|verdict|push_gate|pre_commit|denylist|session_store|help_digest|scoped_law|tree5) passes 270 tests with 0 skipped and 0 xfailed, up from 264 at 7cff6284 purely because the repaired module now enters the selection.

BUG-SURFACE DELTA FOR THE DELTA ITSELF: NET-NEUTRAL, AND THE LEDGER IS CORRECT ABOUT IT. Two filter lines rewritten in place, one import widened, zero branches added, zero production change -- the record's own `diff_direction: net-neutral` and `evidence_diff` match what the diff actually shows, which I verified rather than trusted. The fix is a root-cause fix at the real seam (the test's own path-comparison convention), not a workaround: it does not skip the platform, does not special-case an OS, and adds no flag or branch. It declares `caused_by: none` and cites a reproducible CI run and a named test seam, satisfying the lineage discipline.

=== PRIMARY RANGE, CARRIED FORWARD (62b8dd68..7cff6284) ===

None of the five mandatory REQUEST_CHANGES triggers fires, and each was tested rather than assumed.

SECRETS AND PRIVACY -- CLEAN. The scan over every added line returned 42 hits, all 42 chased individually to a verdict and all 42 false positives in three classes: the word 'token' used as an LLM context-budget unit or as a session mode token; the word 'secret' used as the NAME of the scan engine being relocated; and the regex SOURCE of the credential detector itself. The high-risk subsets each returned ZERO: no operator-home absolute paths, no private-IP literals, no personal e-mail domains, no operator name, no PEM private-key block, and no assignment-shaped credential (a credential keyword followed by a quoted six-plus-character literal). The specs/ additions, which carry the largest text block in the range, likewise returned zero on the same high-risk set.

DENYLIST / PUSH GATE ON THE PRIMARY RANGE -- EXIT 0, in mode 'operator denylist + baseline', fed the real pre-push stdin shape via the absolute venv binary. NOTE FOR THE PUSH OF THIS COMMIT: that run predates the two commits in the delta, and the gate subsequently BLOCKED the push because my own superseded verdict prose enumerated five denylisted private terms. That is the control working exactly as designed -- it caught reviewer prose, not product content -- and it is why this re-issued verdict deliberately describes private markers by category instead of naming them. The coordinator should re-run the gate against the new head before pushing.

PUBLIC-ASSET PRIVACY -- [ok]. `dadaia public doctor` exits 0 and reports '[ok] public-privacy'. I did not stop at the tool's verdict: an independent grep of all 28 touched public asset files for private markers (operator name, operator-home path prefixes, private-IP literals, every sibling repo slug, cloud provider and vendor hostnames, e-mail domains) returned exactly 2 hits, both provably false: an English common noun appearing in doctrine prose about deleting a subsystem, which merely shares a stem with one private repo name, and a template FILENAME that collides with another only under case-insensitive matching. Four new public skills ship in the primary range and none leaks a consumer-specific name, path or host.

DEPENDENCIES -- ZERO NEW CVE SURFACE. poetry.lock untouched; pyproject.toml's only change in the entire range is the version line 0.5.0 -> 0.5.3; no dependency block, extra or constraint edited. setup.cfg's only change ADDS two new CLI modules to the import-linter source_modules list, bringing new code UNDER the layering contract rather than exempting it -- a software-integrity improvement and the inverse of the contract-deletion risk I flagged in the 0.5.2 review. No pip-audit escalation was run for the out-of-range tool venv, per instruction; that pre-existing MEDIUM posture is unchanged and record-only.

TEST INTEGRITY -- NOTHING DISABLED TO GO GREEN. Zero skip/xfail/quarantine markers added; the four keyword hits were prose (an assertion message, a docstring naming a historical bug, a docstring describing string parsing, and a NEGATIVE assertion that silent-skip parsing is gone). Both deleted test files were run down to their paired feature deletion and are PINNED by new assertions that the deleted files stay absent, so the removals cannot silently regress. The two retired doctor rules collapse two implementations of one rule into one, with the surviving rule proven to still fire as an explicit ERROR rather than a silent early return. Net test change +998 LOC.

THE ITEM I TREATED AS THE REAL RISK -- RELOCATING A SECRET SCANNER -- IS PROVABLY LOSSLESS. Moving a credential detector is the change most likely to silently drop a pattern, so I proved equivalence structurally rather than by reading the diff: comparing the pre-move and post-move modules via AST unparse, all three data structures are IDENTICAL (text-suffix allowlist, key-suffix set, rule tuple), with 7 rules before and 7 after in the same order, and the scanner function body is byte-identical after name normalisation. Both detection layers survive (the cert/key-suffix presence layer that catches binary key material, and the content-rule layer over decodable text), as does the redaction contract of returning rule NAMES and never the matched value. Consumer wiring is live, not merely declared: both call sites in the commit-review gate are preserved and a live interpreter confirms the imported alias is the same object as the relocated function, with 7 rules loaded; a committed test pins that identity so a future divergence fails the suite.

THE OTHER SECURITY-SENSITIVE MODULES HOLD. The new injection policy module is a PURE decision table -- no I/O, no env read, no file open -- and, decisively for the untrusted-input question, it never COMPOSES content; it only selects which workspace-local emission the transport builds, so extracting a four-branch state machine out of a 469-line hook reduces the injection surface. The hook's content sources are enumerated and all workspace-local, with no network, subprocess or shell, and the stdin payload used only to resolve a context NAME, never emitted as content. The help digest generator introspects only the live command tree -- command names and docstring first lines, i.e. static source text -- touching no environment variable, subprocess or credential store; the generated artifact scans clean. The new session-record author persists no credential material and REMOVES a dead field rather than adding one. The module that decides PR authorization is UNTOUCHED in the range; the only chokepoint change is an additive, pure, WARN-only advisory that can never block, honouring NO-LOCKS. The new SessionStart matchers point at the SAME hook command via the same builder -- no new executable, privilege or content source.

THE VERDICT PURGE IS A SECURITY IMPROVEMENT AND CLOSES MY OWN PRIOR FINDING. Commit 7cff6284 deletes all six consumed verdict handoffs; a filesystem sweep confirms zero surviving verdict files under specs/. Because the verdict discovery routine reads the archive root as an evidence root and qualifies a candidate on the PR head sha or its first parent, each survivor was a non-expiring approval credential. The range takes that standing-authorization surface from 6 to 0, aligning the code with the law that a consumed verdict is deleted after the merge. This is the direct remediation of the CWE-613 LOW I raised in the 0.5.2 verdict, recorded CLOSED.

GENERATED-FILE LEAKAGE -- NONE, in either the primary range or the delta: nothing under the runtime state directory, no virtualenv, bytecode, cache, log, coverage or test-results artifact is committed.

BUG-SURFACE DELTA (operator standing order) -- REDUCED, unchanged by this delta. The headline +37 net LOC understates the simplification because the range also lands a NEW capability (the CLI help digest, 136 LOC). Excluding it, production is +1890/-1833 = net +57 across 54 files WHILE ADDING 965 LOC of newly extracted single-home modules -- roughly 908 LOC removed from the sprawling homes they replace, i.e. redistribution into named, individually testable owners rather than growth. Measured counters: the container shrinks 607 -> 367 LOC (-240, -40%); a dead protocol-plus-adapter chain is deleted (-443) and pinned deleted by test; two rules that each had two implementations become one rule with one implementation; a never-minted mode token, a dead record field and a dead comparison helper are removed; three hand-built liveness-check copies collapse into one owner; a hand-rolled first-parent walk folds into the single sanctioned seam; a four-branch hook state machine becomes one pure table. Specs shed 1461 net LOC to archival. Tests grow +998 net, several explicitly asserting that the deleted things STAY deleted -- the anti-regression shape the standing order asks for. The delta adds a net-neutral, production-free test repair on top. Open bugs: 0. I found no added flag, special case, second code path or cross-feature reach-in introduced to work around a symptom -- no puxadinho in either range.

findings.message: Delta (7cff6284..47dc1b77) is test-only with zero production change; the separator-agnostic filter fix STRENGTHENS the assertion and restores real coverage on the second OS family, rather than silencing a failure.
findings.detail_md:
**Verified scope.** `git diff --name-only 7cff6284..47dc1b77` yields exactly three paths (the superseded verdict handoff, `specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl`, and `tests/unit/features/specs/test_tree5_shipped_history.py`), and `git diff --name-only 7cff6284..47dc1b77 -- dadaia_workspace/` yields **nothing** -- no production file changed.

**The change.** Two filter lines move from a substring test to a separator-normalised suffix test, and `PurePath` joins an existing `pathlib` import:

```python
-    scoped = [i for i in issues if "releases/AGENTS.md" in (i.path or "")]
+    scoped = [i for i in issues if PurePath(i.path or "").as_posix().endswith("releases/AGENTS.md")]
```

**Why this is a strengthening, not a loosening.** A suffix match is strictly narrower than a substring match, so the filter cannot select more than before. `issue.path` follows the repo convention of an OS-native absolute string, so under the other separator convention the posix substring never matched and the filtered list came back empty -- which made `assert scoped and scoped[0].fixable` fail outright (the observed CI failure) and left the related negative assertion passing for the wrong reason. Normalising restores a genuine match, i.e. restores real coverage on that platform. This is the inverse of the mandatory REQUEST_CHANGES trigger 'a test disabled to hide a live failure'.

**Completeness checked, not assumed.** One further path filter in the same module (the exclusion test, needle `"memory"`) was deliberately left as a substring test. That needle contains no path separator, so it behaves identically under both separator conventions and cannot produce the platform-dependent false negative this bug concerns. The two lines that required conversion are exactly the two converted.

**Suite re-run at the new head.** The repaired module passes 8/8; the security-relevant selector passes 270 tests, 0 skipped, 0 xfailed.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action required. Recorded as evidence that the delta restores coverage rather than suppressing a failure.

findings.message: Process note on the superseded verdict: the pre-push denylist gate blocked it because MY OWN reviewer prose enumerated five private terms while describing the privacy grep. The control worked as designed; this re-issue states private markers by category only.
findings.detail_md:
The blocked content was reviewer narrative, not product content: while documenting which private markers the public-asset grep searched for, the superseded verdict listed the operator denylist terms and a sibling repo slug literally. The pre-push denylist scan refused the push and the terms were replaced with `[redacted]` before commit, with the surrounding content otherwise untouched.

**Why this is worth recording rather than shrugging off.** A security report is committed evidence that travels wherever the repo travels, so it is subject to exactly the same privacy law as the code it reviews. Naming the very terms a denylist exists to suppress -- even to describe a *negative* result -- reintroduces the leak the review was asserting was absent. This verdict therefore describes private markers strictly by CATEGORY (operator name, operator-home path prefixes, private-IP literals, sibling repo slugs, vendor hostnames, e-mail domains) and never by value.

**Consequence for the push of this commit.** The `push-gate-check` exit 0 recorded for the primary range was measured before the two delta commits existed. The gate must be re-run against head `47dc1b77c1350bc9892553335568ee18fc472555` before pushing; the superseded verdict has been deleted from the working tree so it cannot linger as stale evidence.
findings.fix_recommendation: Coordinator: re-run `dadaia ci push-gate-check` with the real pre-push stdin shape against the new head before pushing, and commit the deletion of the superseded verdict together with this file. No product change is implied.

findings.message: Carried forward, positive/closed: the purge of six consumed verdict handoffs takes the standing-authorization surface from 6 to 0, remediating the CWE-613 LOW raised in the 0.5.2 verdict.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-613 (insufficient credential expiration) -- **remediated**, reported as a security improvement.

In the 0.5.2 review I recorded a LOW: the verdict discovery routine globs `*.handoff.json` under **both** the live and the archived release verdict roots, and the covering-verdict check qualifies any candidate whose agent is the security reviewer, whose verdict is APPROVED, and whose `metrics.commit_sha` matches the PR head sha **or its first parent**. Every retained archived verdict was therefore a non-expiring approval credential.

Commit `7cff6284` deletes all six survivors (one under the 0.5.0 archive, five under the 0.5.1 archive). Verified independently: `find specs -path '*verdicts*' -name '*.json'` returns **zero** files. Code and law now agree in practice with the rule that a verdict is consumed once by the merge and deleted after. The prior LOW is recorded CLOSED.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action for this PR. To make the property durable rather than manual, the operator may later have the discovery routine stop treating the archive root as an evidence root, so a future retained verdict cannot become a standing credential again. Governance choice, not a defect; do not bundle into this release.

findings.message: Carried forward: the context-injection WINDOW widens (new SessionStart startup|resume matchers) so content is emitted at session start rather than at first prompt. The content SET and the trust boundary are unchanged.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-829 (inclusion of functionality from an untrusted control sphere) -- **not applicable today**, recorded so the widening is a deliberate, documented decision.

Two Claude Code `SessionStart` matchers (`startup`, `resume`) are added, both pointing at the SAME hook command produced by the SAME builder already used for the existing `compact`/`clear` matchers. No new executable, argument or privilege. The effect is that a fresh session receives the bootstrap at the event rather than at its first prompt.

**Content sources are enumerated and all workspace-local:** the tech-stack digest, the memory catalog digest, the memory index, the sentinel, and the new CLI help digest. There is no network fetch, no subprocess and no shell. The hook stdin payload is consumed only to resolve a context NAME and is never emitted as content.

**Why this is not a finding.** Any actor able to write the injected digest already holds local write access to the workspace and could equally edit the law files, the memory catalog or the tech-stack atom -- all of which were already injected before this range. The trust boundary is identical; only the timing moved earlier. The digest is generated from static command docstrings and is read fail-soft, returning an empty string on any error.
findings.fix_recommendation: None required. For defense in depth the natural control already exists: have the hook skip a digest whose version stamp does not match the installed distribution version instead of injecting it fail-soft, which would also make the staleness note below self-correcting. Do not change this in 0.5.3.

| Symbol | Result |
|---|---|
| text-suffix allowlist | IDENTICAL |

Both detection layers survive -- the cert/key-suffix presence layer that catches binary key material, and the content-rule layer over decodable text -- as does the redaction contract of returning rule NAMES and never the matched value.

The range also commits a test asserting exactly that identity, so a future re-divergence fails the suite.

findings.message: Instance-local only, outside both reviewed ranges: the generated CLI help digest on this machine carries a version stamp older than the release version. Self-healing by design; no security consequence.
findings.detail_md:
Observation only -- the digest file lives under the runtime state directory and is **not** part of either reviewed range (neither range commits anything there).

The on-disk artifact's header stamp names an earlier version than the release version `pyproject.toml` now carries. The generator guards with a stamp check -- it skips the rewrite only when the current stamp is already present in the header, otherwise it regenerates -- so install/reconcile/doctor refresh it. Content is derived exclusively from command names and docstring first lines; scanning the on-disk artifact for credential keywords, key headers, operator-home path prefixes, private-IP literals and personal e-mail domains returns **0 hits**. A stale digest can at worst under-describe the command surface to an agent; it carries no credential and grants no privilege.

Related instance-only residue of the same class: one pre-existing session record still carries a field retired by the new record author, having been written before the fold. Session records carry no credential material (session id, context, mode, release, runtime, pid, bound-at, last-seen-at, ttl), so this is cosmetic drift the TTL reaper clears.
findings.fix_recommendation: Run the projection/reconcile step on this instance after the merge so the digest regenerates against the shipped version. Nothing to change in the repository.
